60202.subject: Geography
60202.question_text:
(a) What is a latitude?

(b) State any three similarities between lines of longitudes and latitudes

(c) Outline any five ways in which lines of longitudes differ from lines of latitudes
60202.explanation:
(a) imaginary lines running from east to west on the surface of the earth OR angular distance of a point on the earth's surface, measured in degrees from the centre of the earthnorth or south of the equator.

(b) both lines are imaginary lines, both lines are angular distances, both lines are measured in degrees from the centre of the earth, both lines are used to calculate distances of places, both lines contain great circles

(c) Lines of longitudes, run from north to south while lines of latitudes run from east  to west, all opposite lines of longitudes form great circles while the equator is the only latitude which forms a great circle. All lines of latitudes are parallel while lines of longitudes converge at the poles, lines of latitude decrease in length from the equator towards the pole while all lines of longitudes are of equal length, lines of longitudes increase in value from the equator towards the pole while lines of longitudes increase in value eastwards and westwards of the greenwich meridian

60204.subject: Geography
60204.question_text:
(a) Define climate

(b) With the aid of a diagram, describe how latitudes influence temperature

(c) Calculate the temperature at a coastal mountain peak of height 6000 metres when the temperature at sea level is 40ºC
60204.explanation:
(a) Climate is the average weather condition of a place taken over a long period of time usually between 30 - 40 years.

(b) temperature decreases from equatorial regions to poles, band of rays from the sun falls vertically over the equatorial region. This band travels through a very short distance at the same time, this band falls or heat up a smaller surface area, this results in the equatorial regions being hotter , the sun's rays fall obliquely on the surface in the temperature latitudes, this band travels a longer distance and much of the heat is lost to clouds, water vapour and dust particles, the rays in the temperate latitudes heat up a larger area than that of the tropics, this results in the temperate latitudes having lower temperatures

(c) Lapse rate is 6.5ºC for every 1000m of ascent.
6000m will have a lapse rate of (6.5 X 6000)ºC 1000 = 39ºC
temperature at sea level = 40ºC
temperature at height 6000m will be (40 - 39)ºC = 1ºC

60206.subject: Geography
60206.question_text:
Describe chemically formed sedimentary rocks under the following headings;
(a) mode of formation (b) examples (c) importance.
60206.explanation:
(a) Materials for formation may be from streams, glaciers, wind:- accumulation of materials derived from other rocks - accumulation over a long period of time - formed through chemical precipitation rocks - hardening of cemented rocks - accumulation laid down in layers/strata over time - variations in thickness of strata.

(b) Sodium chloride (common salt) - limonite - nitrates - gypsum/hydrated calcium sulphate - dolomite - flint - potash - borax - alabasta.

(c) Source of minerals e.g limonite, gypsum and potash - construction materials e.g limestone - ornaments - tourist attraction e.g stalactites and stalagmites in caves - fertilesoil formation e.g potash, nitrate - raw materials for industries e.g gypsum, dolomite, borax - for food e.g rocksalt - medicinal e.g kaolin.

60207.subject: Geography
60207.question_text:
Explain the occurrence of drought under the following headings:
(a) causes (b) area affected (c) effects (d) control
60207.explanation:
(a) prolonged break in rainfall - the presence of high daily temperature - high rate of evapotranspiration - climate change - little or no cloud cover - presence of green house gases - deforestation - overgrazing.

(b) The Sahara desert - Northern Nigeria - senegambia - Northern ghana- mali - mauritania - burkina faso - somalia - niger republic - northern benin republic, etc. Development, logging and paving. - sahelian region - sudan savana region - ethiopia - eritrea

(c) Distorts natural ecosystem - surface river and streams dry up - death of animals - causes condition that allows diseases to thrive e.g cerebrospinal meningitis - loss of crops - result in increase migration - famine - starvation and malnutrition - loss of lives

(d) Irrigation projects - cover cropping - controlled grazing - creation of green belts - reduction in the generation of green house gasses - afforestation - cloud seeding - sensitizing the populace.

60208.subject: Geography
60208.question_text:
(a) List three processes of river erosion

(b) Outline four characteristics of each of the following sections of a river valley: (i) upper course (ii) middle course (iii) lower course.
60208.explanation:
(a) Corrasion/abrasion, solution/corrosion, hydraulic action

(bi) upper course:- *Marks the beginning or source of a river
                              *occurs in highland areas
                              *main river flows swiftly down the steep slopes
                              *headward erosion also occurs

(ii) middle course:- *lateral erosion is dominant over vertical erosion
                              *valleys are widened
                              *increased load of the river
                              *dominant work is transported 

(iii) lower course:- *main work is deposition 
                             *there is active lateral erosion 
                             *increased volume of rivers from addition by tributaries
                             *speed of the river is greatly slackened
